text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: P1 alert - spike in 502 responses from ELB pool in us-west-1b. Source: elb-usw1b-prod-edge, started 1768123420 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Paging morgan (oncall) and sophia (oncall) - P1 - ELB 502 surge - see alert group 0x9f3
morgan (oncall): I’m on it. seeing elevated 502s and instance healthcheck flaps for backend fleet in us-west-1b. grabbing logs.
ryan (svc-eng): Confirm we just deployed a config change ~40m ago? No changes to ELB config from app side per my last deploy.
alin (infra): AWS console metrics show EBS API 5xx/Throttling spike in us-west-1b and a small jump in EC2 instance status checks failing. suspect EBS detach/attach errors.
incident-bot: Automated note: ELB backend unhealthy count > 45 (threshold 5). Latency increased 2.1x.
morgan (oncall): collecting host logs: checking instance i-0a1b2c3d in us-west-1b - showing repeated errors attaching volumes:
```
2026-06-01T12:02:17Z kernel: Unable to attach volume vol-0abcd1234: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
2026-06-01T12:02:18Z cloud-init: Mount failed for /data - device not ready
2026-06-01T12:03:05Z systemd: Started ELB healthcheck responder
2026-06-01T12:03:32Z app: upstream returned 502 bad gateway
```
sophia (oncall): ok that matches the AWS metrics I'm seeing. health checks failing because application can't reach disk-mounted state. ELB marks instances OUT, then traffic gets 502s.
ryan (svc-eng): Any retention/caching issues that would explain multiple volumes detaching? We didn't change EBS settings.
alin (infra): Looks like a regional EBS API throttling event — probably a backend control plane problem. I opened AWS support case (case# 1234567890). AWS acknowledged increased EBS API errors in us-west-1b and are investigating.
aws-support: Support: we've validated elevated EBS API error rates in us-west-1b affecting Attach/Detach. Engineering is investigating backend throttles. ETA unknown. Will update.
morgan (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) Remove us-west-1b from Route53 weighted set (shift traffic to us-west-1a and us-east-1), 2) Put affected instances in us-west-1b into maintenance (disable ELB targets), 3) If necessary, fail traffic to us-west-2. Doable?
sophia (oncall): agree. initiating quick traffic shift to reduce customer impact. I'll update Route53 weights to drop us-west-1b to 0 and increase us-west-1a/us-east-1.
alin (infra): Command I’ll run (Route53 change):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-1b","Weight":0,"TTL":30}}, {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-1a","Weight":60,"TTL":30}}, {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":40,"TTL":30}}]}'
```
alin (infra): Executed at 1768123520. Route53 change submitted. Expected propagation ~30s TTL but client caches vary.
morgan (oncall): Also starting ELB deregistration for targets in us-west-1b to stop health flapping and reduce retry traffic. Running: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:usw1b:abcdef --targets Id=i-...`
ryan (svc-eng): Will disable auto-scaler for us-west-1b so it doesn't trigger more attach attempts until AWS resolves.
sophia (oncall): Noted. I'm posting a public status update to status.redwood: "We are experiencing degraded API responses from a subset of hosts in us-west-1. Traffic temporarily shifted while we mitigate. Root cause is an AWS EBS API issue affecting volume operations in us-west-1b." :writing_hand:
morgan (oncall): Customer impact: estimated 20-30% of API traffic hitting increased 502s for ~8 minutes before we started mitigation. Major consumer alerts from two enterprise customers.
dev-platform: Flagging feature flags that route heavy batch jobs to other regions — throttling those now to reduce load.
aws-support: Update: investigating EBS backend throttles; recommending draining nodes rather than rebooting to avoid repeated attach attempts.
sophia (oncall): Draining completed for registered targets in us-west-1b at 1768123630. Health check failures dropped after drain finishes. 502 rate falling.
morgan (oncall): Metrics: 502 rate peaked at 18% of requests, down to 1.2% now. Latency returning to normal.
alin (infra): AWS indicates mitigations on their side in progress; case# 1234567890 updated. They suggest we keep volumes stable and avoid detach/attach operations for now.
ryan (svc-eng): We should avoid any ops that touch volumes in the region. Confirming no scheduled jobs that will do snapshots or resizes in next 2 hours.
aws-support: Note: We are continuing to monitor EBS attach/detach API 5xx rates. We'll post when error rate is within normal bounds.
morgan (oncall): Taking incident to monitoring state. Sophia, can you take 30m watch and then hand back? I'll create the incident ticket and post RCA template.
sophia (oncall): Taking watch. I'll escalate if we see any regression.
incident-bot: Incident state updated -> monitoring. Severity: SEV1 -> downgraded to SEV2 after traffic shift and drain.
morgan (oncall): Action items for postmortem: 1) Add playbook step to automatically reduce Route53 weight for AZ-level infrastructure degradations, 2) Add alert to detect EBS API throttling earlier, 3) Test cross-region failover runbooks. Assigning to dev-platform and infra.
dev-platform: Will take item 3.
alin (infra): Taking item 2; will follow up with AWS trust advisor on quota and throttling patterns.
ryan (svc-eng): Will add a safety throttle to our auto-scaler to avoid concurrent attach storms on partial-region events.
morgan (oncall): Incident ticket created: INC-2026-061-013. Notifying customer success for enterprise outreach.
sophia (oncall): Thanks team. I'll watch for 30m then close if stable.
incident-bot: Final note at 1768123980: 502 rate stable <2%, ELB target count normalized, AWS continuing backend fix.
